name: Ashy Minivet
rangeDescription: Northeastern asia; winters to philippines and indonesia
description: Slender, long-tailed gray songbird, usually seen in small to medium-sized flocks. Male has a distinct black-and-white head pattern, of which the female has a paler gray version.

name: Mouse-gray Flycatcher
rangeDescription: West of the andes in southwestern colombia, western ecuador, and northwestern peru (southward to southwestern cajamarca)
description: Small, dull-colored flycatcher fond of lightly wooded areas, dry savanna, and forest edge. Its brownish-gray plumage, streaky breast, and buffy wingbars separate it from other similar species.

name: Scimitar-winged Piha
rangeDescription: Southern peru (cordillera apolobamba of puno) and western bolivia
description: Rare cotinga found along the east slope of the Andes in Bolivia and southern Peru. Plumage is mostly gray with chestnut flanks and rump.

name: Gray Pratincole
rangeDescription: Rivers of mali to cameroon, western democratic republic of the congo, and northwestern angola
description: A compact, elegant pratincole, mostly pale gray above with a warm buffy nape that sometimes extends to the breast and a striking black-and-white face pattern; the legs and base of the bill are reddish. In flight, the striking black-and-white patterning in the wings and tail is unique.

name: Toro Olive-Greenbul
rangeDescription: Southern south sudan, eastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, far western kenya, and far northwestern tanzania
description: A drab, long-tailed brownish greenbul. The upperparts are brown and the underparts paler olive-gray.

name: Enggano Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Enggano island (off southwestern sumatra)
description: Small rufous-brown scops-owl with bright yellow eyes and a whitish “X” on the face. Endemic to the island of Enggano, where it is the only resident scops-owl; migrating Oriental Scops-Owl may stop over on the island, but are readily distinguished by their larger size, more well-defined facial disc, and lack of prominent white facial markings.

name: Blue-banded Toucanet
rangeDescription: Andes of eastern peru (huánuco) to southern bolivia (santa cruz, chuquisaca)
description: Small green toucan of humid montane forest. Blue chest band is distinctive but can be difficult to see; notice also the bluish coloration in its face and bill and the yellowish bill tip.

name: Guadalupe Murrelet
rangeDescription: San benito island and guadalupe island (off baja california)
description: Small black-and-white diving seabird, unlikely to be seen from land. Usually found as singles or pairs, well offshore, and not usually associating with other seabirds.

name: Mangrove Pitta
rangeDescription: Southern bangladesh to malay peninsula, sumatra, bangka island, and riau archipelago
description: The huge crab-smashing bill of this mangrove specialist sets it apart from all other pittas. Brightly colored with a black mask, green-and-black wings, and a yellow belly.

name: Blue-eyed Cockatoo
rangeDescription: New ireland and new britain (eastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A large, bulky white parrot with a tall yellow-and-white crest that it often raises when perched and bright blue skin around the eyes. In flight, underwing and undertail washed yellowish.

name: Southern Red Bishop
rangeDescription: Western and southern angola, southern and eastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, kenya, and tanzania, southward to south africa
description: A small, dumpy sparrow-like weaver. The breeding male is a mix of velvety vermilion and black; the narrow black forecrown is diagnostic.

name: Kamchatka Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Incompletely known; breeds southern kamchatka, sakhalin, kuril islands, and northeastern hokkaido; winters at least to indonesia
description: Small songbird, essentially identical in plumage to Arctic Warbler and Japanese Leaf Warbler. A late spring migrant, often moving up the Chinese coast from Southeast Asia in mid- to late May.

name: Cassin's Sparrow
rangeDescription: Arid southwestern usa and adjacent northern mexico; winters to central mexico
description: Dull sparrow lacking distinctive patterns. Found in grasslands with scattered bushes.

name: Chatham Islands Oystercatcher
rangeDescription: Chatham islands (chatham, mangere, rangatira, and pitt)
description: Stocky wader with distinctive pied plumage, red eye surrounded by orange eye-ring, orange bill, and pink legs and feet in adults. Juvenile birds have paler skin and dark tip to bill.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Chestnut-capped Puffbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to venezuela, northern bolivia, and western amazonian brazil
description: Attractive small puffbird of lowland rainforest. White below, reddish brown above, with a black mask and single black breast band.

name: Hooded Crane
rangeDescription: Siberia and northwestern manchuria; winters to eastern china, korea, and japan
description: A small, somber-colored crane of expansive agricultural fields and wetlands. Rare outside of its main wintering grounds in southern Japan, western Korea, and eastern China, where it gathers in small family units as well as massive flocks.

name: Black-fronted Ground-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Andes of chile and argentina; winters northward to southern peru (arequipa)
description: Breeds locally in the high Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina; migrates north in winter. Favors bleak rocky and stony slopes, adjacent bogs, and lakeshores; often in same areas as other ground-tyrant species.

name: Andaman Treepie
rangeDescription: Dense forest of andaman islands
description: A slender, medium-sized dark bird with a long tail. The face, wings, and tail are black, while the underparts and back are reddish-brown.

name: Orange-fronted Plushcrown
rangeDescription: Tropical southeastern colombia to northern bolivia and western amazonian brazil
description: Small, yellowish-tan bird. Orange face is unique, but sometimes difficult to see; a more obvious field mark is its bright orange legs.

name: White-fronted Falconet
rangeDescription: Forest of northern borneo
description: Tiny, compact, black-and-white falcon. Black above, with a white chest and pale orangish belly.
